Simulate synthetic GC-MS chromatograms with ground-truth signal + background

Source: R/simulate_GCMS.R
simulate_GCMS.Rd

`simulate_GCMS()` draws \(k\) compounds from an EI reference library `S` (rows = compounds, columns = m/z values, e.g. 41-298) and generates an \(n \times m\) chromatogram `D` whose signal is the sum of k Gaussian peaks (`W_true H_true`) and a smooth, monotonically increasing B-spline background (`W_background*bg_scale H_background`).

Usage

simulate_GCMS(
  n = 10000,
  k = 500,
  S = NULL,
  peak_width_range = c(3, 5),
  mean_beta = 10000,
  sd_logbeta = 1,
  width_height_coef = 3,
  rt_height_coef = 0.02,
  sample_nr = 1,
  rt_drift_coef = 0.001,
  bg_scale = mean_beta/10,
  family = c("poisson", "gaussian"),
  sd_noise = if (match.arg(family) == "gaussian") 1 else NULL,
  seed_compounds = 123,
  seed_peaks = 456
)

Arguments

n

Integer >= 1. Number of time points (rows).

k

Integer >= 1. Number of compounds/peaks.

S

Spectral library. If `NULL` the example data `data(simulated_spectra)` (2000 spectra x 258 m/z values) is loaded.

peak_width_range

Length-2 numeric. Uniform base range for Gaussian peak width sigma (*before* any height-coupling is applied and on time point scale).

mean_beta, sd_logbeta

Parameters of the log-normal height distribution.

width_height_coef

Numeric >= 0. Multiplicative widening: $$\sigma_j \leftarrow \sigma_j\bigl[1+\texttt{coef}\,h_j\bigr]$$ where \(h_j=(\beta_j-\min\beta)/(\max\beta-\min\beta)\).

rt_height_coef

Numeric. Positive values push high peaks to slightly larger RTs: $$c_j \leftarrow c_j \bigl[1+\texttt{rt\_height\_coef}\,h_j\bigr]$$

sample_nr

Integer >= 1. Injection/order number.

rt_drift_coef

Numeric. Additive drift in *time points* per injection: \(c_j \leftarrow c_j + \texttt{rt\_drift\_coef}\, (\texttt{sample\_nr}-1)\).

bg_scale

Numeric >= 0. Multiplicative factor applied to the whole B-spline background.

family

`"poisson"` (default) or `"gaussian"`.

sd_noise

s.d. of additive Gaussian noise (`family="gaussian"`).

seed_compounds

Integer seed controlling which library spectra are drawn.

seed_peaks

Integer seed for all other random quantities (heights, widths, noise, ...).

Value

A list with matrices:

D

Observed chromatogram (signal + background + noise) (dense matrix).

D_true

Noiseless signal `W_true H_true + W_background H_background` (dense matrix).

W_true, H_true

Elution profiles and EI spectra of the *k* peaks (sparse matrices).

W_background, H_background

Smooth B-spline background bases and spectra (sparse matrices).

k_background

Number of B-spline basis columns (`max(2, n/1000)`).

centres, widths, heights

Peak parameters after all applied height/RT/drift adjustments.

widths_base

Base compound width before intensity-based broadening.

compound_idx

Row indices of `S` that were selected.

sample_nr, rt_drift_coef, width_height_coef, rt_height_coef

Echoed.

Details

  • A compound-specific base width \(\sigma_{0}\) is drawn once when the compound is first selected from the library.

  • In subsequent simulated chromatograms the same compound retains the same \(\sigma_{0}\), but the effective width becomes $$\sigma \;=\; \sigma_{0}\Bigl(1 + \texttt{width\_height\_coef}\,h_{\mathrm{norm}}\Bigr),$$ so it can still broaden or narrow in proportion to its (possibly resampled) peak height.

Gaussian peak width and RT can be coupled to peak height; an additional *chromatographic drift* proportional to the injection number `sample_nr` is also included. Independent random seeds allow you to keep the same compounds while resampling peak heights (or vice-versa).

Reference library

`S` must contain - column names (character) for the m/z channels (e.g. `"41":"298"`), and - attribute `attr(S, "RT")` for the retention times *(numeric, unit: mins)*.

Author

Tom Wenseleers tom.wenseleers@kuleuven.be \ Laboratory of Socioecology and Social Evolution, KU Leuven \ https://bio.kuleuven.be/eeb/tw/research \ ORCID: 0000-0002-1434-861X

Examples

data(simulated_spectra)
sim <- simulate_GCMS(n = 10000,
                     k = 500,
                     S = simulated_spectra,
                     peak_width_range = c(3, 5),
                     mean_beta  = 1e4,
                     sd_logbeta = 1,
                     width_height_coef = 3,
                     rt_height_coef    = 0.02,
                     sample_nr = 1,
                     rt_drift_coef = 0.001,
                     bg_scale = 100,
                     family = "poisson")
plotmat(sim$D, 
        xlab = "Time (min)", 
        ylab = "Mass (m/z)", 
        main = "Simulated GC/MS chromatogram")
